name: Twin to Twin Transfusion Syndrome

criteria.description: Polyhydramnios in the recipient twin with deepest vertical pocket >8 cm before 20 weeks or >10 cm after 20 weeks
Oligohydramnios in the donor twin with deepest vertical pocket <2 cm
Absent or small bladder in the donor twin on ultrasound
Abnormal Doppler studies in either twin (e.g., absent or reversed end-diastolic flow)
Significant discordance in fetal size or growth between twins

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of polyhydramnios in recipient twin and oligohydramnios in donor twin (major criteria) on ultrasound
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on ultrasound findings in monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies.

pathognomonic.notes: Excess amniotic fluid accumulation around recipient twin
searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in recipient twin

pathognomonic.notes: Reduced amniotic fluid volume around donor twin
searchTerms: low amniotic fluid in donor twin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or small bladder in donor twin
pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of decreased urine output due to hypovolemia
searchTerms: missing or small bladder in donor twin

common.symptomName: Abnormal Doppler velocimetry in umbilical artery
common.notes: May show absent or reversed end-diastolic flow
searchTerms: abnormal blood flow in umbilical artery

occasional.notes: Often due to polyhydramnios and uterine overdistension
Due to hypovolemia and blood loss
searchTerms: low fetal blood count in donor twin
donor twin with low red cells

occasional.notes: Less common than in recipient twin
Secondary to polyhydramnios causing diaphragmatic elevation

rare.symptomName: Fetal demise of one or both twins
rare.notes: Severe cases may result in intrauterine death
searchTerms: death of one or both twins before birth

rare.notes: Due to hypoxia or ischemia following acute hemodynamic changes

laboratory: Elevated maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein may be present
No specific maternal laboratory markers diagnostic
imaging: Ultrasound showing discordant amniotic fluid volumes (polyhydramnios and oligohydramnios)
Absent or small bladder in donor twin on ultrasound
Doppler studies showing abnormal umbilical artery flow
Cardiomegaly and hydrops fetalis on fetal ultrasound
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; condition related to placental vascular anastomoses
other: Monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy is a prerequisite

distinguishingFeatures: Growth restriction primarily in one twin without volume imbalance
Doppler studies showing middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity differences

redFlags: Rapidly progressing polyhydramnios in recipient twin
Absent bladder in donor twin on ultrasound
Signs of fetal hydrops or cardiomegaly in recipient twin
references: Quintero RA, et al. Staging of twin-twin transfusion syndrome. J Perinatol. 1999.
American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Practice Bulletin No. 169: Multifetal Gestations. Obstet Gynecol. 2016.
